chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from his father, from Muyassar, who said:

Anger was mentioned in the presence of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, a man becomes angry and is not pleased until he enters the Fire. Therefore, whoever of men gets angry upon a people while he is standing, let him sit down immediately, for the filth of Satan will depart from him. And whoever of men gets angry upon a relative, let him draw near to him and let him touch him, for the relative, when touched, calms down.'
ai.seo_question: What are the physical actions recommended in Shia hadith to control anger and prevent entering Hellfire?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the spiritual danger of anger to its physical manifestation, prescribing immediate bodily adjustments to disrupt the Shaytan's influence. The instruction to sit down while standing or to touch a relative (silat al-rahim) serves as a tangible mechanism to cool the heart, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the interplay between physical action and spiritual state in self-purification (tazkiyah).
